fields.acceptance: A testscript runs rhiza daemon --once against a fake Rex: the run's driver starts as a rhiza run start --foreground process with the change set's ID (and --autonomous only under rhiza daemon --once --autonomous), with no rex window new for it and no new queue entry, a line the child itself prints (step build/build: entered) lands in the run's log file, and rhiza run ls shows the run live after the daemon has exited; testscripts for plan requests and for resume see the daemon start a request's plan run as a detached rhiza run start --foreground --workflow plan --new ... --request <request> and an interrupted run's driver as a detached rhiza run resume --foreground <run>, with no rex window new for either
fields.statement: The daemon starts each run as a detached rhiza run start --foreground <change set> process, starts a request's plan run as a detached rhiza run start --foreground --workflow plan --new <intent> --request <request> process (with --milestone for a milestone request), and resumes or continues one as a detached rhiza run resume --foreground <run> process, in the repo and outside Rex, adding --autonomous only when the daemon was started with --autonomous, with output in the run's log file under .git/rhiza, so no Rex tab holds a run's driver, the child drives the run rather than queueing it again, and a run still outlives the daemon; the daemon reaps each such child when it exits, so a driver that dies shows as interrupted, not live; it replaces daemon-run-tabs, which it retires

set.acceptance: A testscript runs rhiza daemon --once against a fake Rex with REX_SESSION unset: when rex session ls lacks rhiza-<repo> the daemon creates it once and every detached run driver it starts carries REX_SESSION=rhiza-<repo>; with the session present it creates none; with REX_SESSION set to another session those drivers still carry rhiza-<repo>
set.statement: Every Rex tab the daemon's runs open (agent tabs; plan-request runs and run drivers start headless, outside Rex, by daemon-headless-run-drivers) opens in the Rex session rhiza-<repo>, named after the main checkout's folder, which the daemon creates on its Rex server when missing and passes as REX_SESSION to every run driver it starts, so it needs no Rex tab or REX_SESSION of its own

set.acceptance: A testscript with a fixture journal that is unfinished and names a dead process runs rhiza daemon --once twice with a fake Rex: the first starts one detached rhiza run resume --foreground on that run and journals it, the second (with the run interrupted again) starts none; a failed run's journal gets no resume.
set.statement: The daemon resumes an interrupted run whose change set is accepted once, as a detached rhiza run resume --foreground <run> process outside Rex (daemon-headless-run-drivers), and journals that resume in the run's journal; it leaves alone an interrupted run whose change set is not accepted, a run interrupted again after that resume, which the inbox lists as a run the daemon gave up on, and every failed run, which the inbox lists as failed.
